wing: 41st Combat Bombardment Wing (low group, per 303rd BG mission report table)
dispatched_note: 384th BG mission #32 record: 21 aircraft assigned (Personnel Roster: 21 aircraft, 190 combat personnel); 2 were ground spares that did not fly, so 19 sorties flown. Sortie summary: 5 completed, 1 returned early (combat credit), 4 aborted after takeoff, 3 crashed in Allied territory (crews bailed out over England on return; bombed target), 6 failed to return (MACRs 838, 839, 840, 841, 842, 1038). The mission narrative says "six aircraft aborted" (likely counts the 4 aborts + early return + another) and the group's Sept 2020 newsletter says 21 took off, 6 lost, 3 bailed out over England, 5 aborted - these counts conflict slightly with the sortie table; the sortie-level table is used here. The 303rd BG Mission 78 report table lists the 384BG as low group of the 41st CBW with 16 aircraft (lead 379BG 17, high 303BG 19; wing leader Col. Rohr) - likely the planned/formed figure, versus 19 sorties in the 384th records.
lost_note: lost = 6 Failed To Return (enemy action). A further 3 aircraft (42-3037, 42-5852, 42-29784) were abandoned over England on return = 9 aircraft lost to the group in total.

research_gaps: Ranks: 384th BG person pages record lowest/highest rank while with the group plus some dated promotion entries; rank on 14 Oct 1943 is set only where a single rank was recorded or dated promotions allow derivation. Others left null with the recorded range in notes.
Waist gunner side (left/right) is not recorded in the loading lists; recorded as "waist".
Nicknames come from the 384th BG aircraft database (not date-specific); no photographic evidence for nose art on 14 Oct 1943 was checked. nose_art left null throughout.

Formation positions: only group lead (42-30026, with Capt. George W. Harris as Commander) and High Squadron lead (42-3429, aborted) are recorded in sortie comments. Full formation chart not located; the 384th site photo gallery category "Combat Mission Records and Plans" (photos.384thbombgroup.com/index.php?/category/4718) may contain the formation diagram but was not parsed.
Block numbers not recorded in sources consulted (384th aircraft pages may carry them; not checked per aircraft).
americanairmuseum.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; only search-result titles were used as cross-checks for aircraft names/MACR of 42-3216, 42-30196, 42-3037, 42-31059.
Wounded crewmen who returned (e.g. 1st/2nd Lt. Joseph L. Bedsole, 42-29809) are recorded with fate "wounded"; nature of wounds not researched.

b17flyingfortress.de lists 42-30040 (Piccadilly Commando, MACR 837) under the 384th for this mission; the 384th BG aircraft page shows it was transferred to the 96th BG (337BS, AW-A) on 6 Jul 1943 and was lost with the 96th on 14 Oct 1943 (crashed Avincourt, France) - NOT a 384th sortie. Likewise b17flyingfortress.de attributes 42-29784 and 42-29867 to the 381st as well; 384th loading lists show both flew with the 384th.

Earlier draft placed the 384th in the 40th CBW from a newsletter summary mentioning Col. Peaslee; the 303rd BG report table places it in the 41st CBW. Peaslee (former 384th CO) led the 1st Air Division / 40th CBW flying with the 92nd BG.
